'''Fumiko Futamura''' is a Japanese-American mathematician known for her work on the [[Perspective (graphical)|mathematics of perspective]] and perspective drawing. She is a professor of mathematics at [[Southwestern University]] in [[Georgetown, Texas]], and Lord Chair in Mathematics and Computer Science at Southwestern.

==Education and career==
Futamura is originally from Japan, and emigrated with her family to [[Kentucky]] when she was five years old.{{r|wonderland}} She grew up in an artistic family,{{r|wonderland|initium}} and despite a talent for mathematics preferred creating art in various mediums.{{r|initium}} She entered the [[University of Louisville]] intending to study art there, but switched to mathematics after taking [[linear algebra]] in her sophomore year, discovering the beauty in mathematical proofs, and becoming convinced by faculty mentor Steven Seif that mathematics could be viewed as a form of art.{{r|wonderland|initium}}

She met her future husband, YouTube mathematics tutor Patrick Jones, when they were both mathematics students at the University of Louisville.{{r|jones}} After Futamura graduated [[summa cum laude]] in 2002, with a senior thesis on graphical methods in geometry supervised by Robert Powers,{{r|cv}} she and Jones both entered graduate study at [[Vanderbilt University]]. Jones dropped out of the graduate program to become a full-time mathematics tutor, but Futamura continued,{{r|jones}} earning a master's degree and completing her Ph.D. in 2007. Her dissertation, ''Symmetrically Localized Frames, Localized Operators and Their Application to the Construction of Localized Hilbert and Banach Frames'', was supervised by [[Akram Aldroubi]],{{r|cv|mg}} and involved the theory of [[Frame (linear algebra)|frames]] in linear algebra.{{r|wonderland}}

In order to continue her work combining mathematics with the creative arts, Futamura decided to teach mathematics at a [[liberal arts college]] rather than go into industry or take a research university position.{{r|wonderland}} She joined the Southwestern University faculty as an assistant professor in 2007, was tenured as an associate professor in 2013, and became a full professor in 2018. In the same year she became department chair.{{r|cv}}

==Writing and recognition==
Futamura won the [[Carl B. Allendoerfer Award]] of the [[Mathematical Association of America]] in 2018, with Southwestern student Robert Lehr, for their 2017 article "A New Perspective on Finding the Viewpoint".{{r|allen1|allen2}}

She is the coauthor of the book ''Perspective and Projective Geometry'', with [[Annalisa Crannell]] and Marc Frantz, published by Princeton University Press in 2019.{{r|perpro}}
